newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Death toll rises to four in Lisbon bridge accident.
newsitem.headline: Death toll rises to four in Lisbon bridge accident.

text.p: The death toll from an accident at a Lisbon bridge construction project has risen to four, including two French engineers, and two men were believed still missing, construction company officials said on Friday.
Three bodies, including a second Portuguese worker, were recovered in the early hours of Friday after a metal girder collapsed on Thursday, plunging 40 metres into the river Tagus.
The Portuguese foreman in charge of work in that part of the bridge had already been reported killed in the accident in which eight people were also injured.
One of the injured, a British engineer, was in a deep coma in a Lisbon hospital but the others were in less serious condition, hospital officials.
A spokeswoman for Lusoponte, the Anglo-French consortium building the 18-km (11-mile) bridge, named the two dead Frenchmen as Etienne Muller and Jermome Cornielle.
Some 3,500 people are employed on building the bridge over the Tagus river north of Lisbon which is one of Europe's largest construction projects.
Work around the area where the accident occurred was halted while an official inquiry was carried out.
